title: Ἀγαλματοπώλης
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 2 (= Perry 99). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ξύλινόν τις Ἑρμῆν κατασκευάσας καὶ προσενεγκὼν εἰς ἀγορὰν ἐπώλει· μηδενὸς δὲ ὠνητοῦ προσιόντος, ἐκκαλέσασθαί τινας βουλόμενος, ἐβόα ὡς ἀγαθοποιὸν δαίμονα καὶ κέρδους δωρητικὸν πιπράσκει.
sentences.tr: Xylinon tis Hermēn kataskeuasas kai prosenenkōn eis agoran epōlei· mēdenos de ōnētou prosiontos, ekkalesasthai tinas boulomenos, eboa hōs agathopoion daimona kai kerdous dōrētikon pipraskei.
sentences.l: A wooden Hermes someone having made and having brought into the market-place was selling; and no buyer coming near, wishing to call some people to him, he kept crying that he was selling a divinity that does good and bestows gain.
sentences.i: A man made a wooden Hermes, brought it to market, and offered it for sale; and since no buyer came near, wanting to draw a few people out he began shouting that what he had for sale was a spirit that did good and granted profit.
sentences.n: μηδενὸς ὠνητοῦ προσιόντος is a genitive absolute: a noun and a participle set in the genitive, standing free of the main clause to give the circumstances — 'no buyer coming forward.' It is the workhorse construction of these fables; you will see it constantly. ἐπώλει and ἐβόα are imperfects: he was trying to sell, he kept shouting. Hermes was the god of trade and of the lucky find (ἕρμαιον, a windfall), which is why his statue is the one a market-seller can advertise as a bringer of gain.

sentences.t: Τῶν δὲ παρατυχόντων τινὸς εἰπόντος πρὸς αὐτόν· « Ὦ οὗτος, καὶ τί τοῦτον τοιοῦτον ὄντα πωλεῖς, δέον τῶν παρ’ αὐτοῦ ὠφελειῶν ἀπολαύειν ; » ἀπεκρίνατο ὅτι ἐγὼ μὲν ταχείας ὠφελείας τινὸς δέομαι, αὐτὸς δὲ βραδέως εἴωθε τὰ κέρδη περιποιεῖν.
sentences.tr: Tōn de paratychontōn tinos eipontos pros auton· « Ō houtos, kai ti touton toiouton onta pōleis, deon tōn par’ autou ōpheleiōn apolauein ; » apekrinato hoti egō men tacheias ōpheleias tinos deomai, autos de bradeōs eiōthe ta kerdē peripoiein.
sentences.l: And one of the bystanders having said to him: « You there, and why do you sell him, being such a one, when you ought to be enjoying the benefits from him ? » he answered that I for my part need some quick benefit, but he is accustomed to procure his gains slowly.
sentences.i: One of the bystanders said to him, « You there — why do you sell him, when he is what you say he is, and you ought to be enjoying the benefits he gives ? » He answered, « I have need of some benefit quickly; he is accustomed to bring his profits in slowly. »
sentences.n: δέον is the accusative absolute — the neuter participle of the impersonal δεῖ standing alone, 'it being necessary' — here concessive: 'when you ought to.' Ὦ οὗτος is a blunt hail, roughly 'hey, you there.' The ὅτι after ἀπεκρίνατο is recitative: it introduces the man's own words unchanged, so the Greek keeps the first person ἐγώ where English would open quotation marks. The Greek question mark is the semicolon-shaped ; and Chambry, printing in France, sets a space before it.

sentences.t: Πρὸς ἄνδρα αἰσχροκερδῆ μηδὲ θεῶν πεφροντικότα ὁ λόγος εὔκαιρος.
sentences.tr: Pros andra aischrokerdē mēde theōn pephrontikota ho logos eukairos.
sentences.l: Against a man shamefully-greedy and not even having given the gods a thought, the story is timely.
sentences.i: The story is well aimed at a man greedy for base gain, one who has no regard even for the gods.
sentences.n: Not 'the story shows that…' but a statement of whom the story suits: πρός with the accusative, 'with reference to, aimed at,' and εὔκαιρος, 'well-timed, apt.' αἰσχροκερδής (αἰσχρός + κέρδος) is a standing term of abuse, greed of the shameful kind. πεφροντικότα is a perfect participle of φροντίζω with the genitive: he has never once given the gods a thought.
